title: Lobster Trap: OpenClaw in Containers from Local to K8s and Back — Sally Ann O'Malley, Red Hat
talk_summary: A Red Hat engineer describes running OpenClaw agents in Podman containers locally and lifting the same setup to Kubernetes/OpenShift, emphasizing secret refs, mounted agent directories, and volume-backed state. The talk is mostly a demo of her personal installer rather than measured engineering results.

takeaways.technique: Double secret-ref indirection for API keys
takeaways.what_they_do: Store API keys as Podman/K8s secrets, mount them into the container, and have the agent config reference them via secret refs rather than plaintext env vars, so keys never appear in logs or config files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: my API keys are pointer to a secret ref to the outside secret

takeaways.technique: Containerized agent runtime with mounted agent directory
takeaways.what_they_do: Build one image per agent runtime and mount a directory of tools, skills, and MCP servers at startup so the environment is reproducible and identical across laptop, x86, Mac, and K8s.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can set up a whole agent directory with maybe you run some tools, some skills, some MCP servers ... mount that whole thing into your container

takeaways.what_they_do: Give the agent SSH keys and known_hosts to a target workspace so all its shell commands execute remotely in that workspace rather than on the host.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You give it SSH keys and known hosts to to wherever you want and it it runs all of its commands in that workspace

takeaways.technique: Curated baseline agent image fanned out to team
takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain a company-approved baseline (approved MCP servers, auth, team skills, shared drive access) that new agents/teammates inherit, then personalize per instance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just you get your your base ... company approved MCP servers, your authentication that is approved through your company

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep all runtime state in a named Podman volume (or K8s PVC) so backup and recovery operate on one contained volume rather than scattered host files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of my runtime state lives in a nice contained Podman volume

takeaways.technique: OpenTelemetry + Jaeger tracing for agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Optionally wire an OTel collector with Jaeger into the agent runtime to trace runs (she admits she didn't test it in the demo).
takeaways.evidence_quote: I was like, "I'm going to give the option to set up an Open Telemetry collector with Jaeger."
